name: noticeH – Notice Board & Announcements
author: habibhq

sections.description:
noticeH is a notice board and announcement plugin for WordPress. Publish notices for your school, college, university, office, mosque, society or community, and show them on any page as a card grid, table, list, timeline, slider or scrolling news ticker.

Each notice can have a priority badge, a reference number, an expiry date and file attachments, so official notices look official and old ones disappear on time.

Common uses:

  • A school or university notice board with exam schedules, holiday notices and results.
  • Office and HR announcements with reference numbers and PDF attachments.
  • A scrolling news ticker of the latest notices on your home page.
  • Community, society or mosque announcements that expire automatically.

Six notice board layouts

  • Card grid with category filters, search and priority badges.
  • Table with reference number, category, priority, date and a Read More button.
  • List and timeline views.
  • Slider (Swiper carousel).
  • Cubed news ticker that scrolls notices, with a hover preview card.

Built for official notices

  • Pinned notices: keep important announcements at the top with a badge and a coloured border.
  • Priority levels: mark notices as Normal, Important or Urgent, each with its own badge colour.
  • Automatic reference numbers such as #REF-2026-001, or type your own.
  • Expiry dates: expired notices can be hidden, kept in the archive, or moved to the trash automatically.
  • Attachments: add files from the Media Library, or link files stored on Google Drive, Dropbox or another site.
  • Search and filters by keyword, category, year and month.

Easy to place and style

  • Gutenberg block and the [noticeh_board] shortcode, which works in any theme or page builder that accepts shortcodes, including Elementor, Divi and Beaver Builder.
  • Colours, font sizes and labels set from noticeH → Settings, with colour pickers.
  • Theme templates: copy any template into your-theme/noticeh/ to change the markup.
  • Single notice pages with print and share buttons for Facebook, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, email and copy link.

Import, export and feeds

  • CSV import and export of notices, with a sample CSV template.
  • RSS feed of notices at /feed/noticeh/.
  • Sample notices you can import in one click to try the layouts, and remove again.

Privacy

Font Awesome, Swiper and AOS are bundled with the plugin, so nothing loads from a CDN. The only external service is Google Fonts, which is off by default (see External services below).

External services

noticeH can load fonts from Google Fonts. This is off by default and only happens if a site administrator turns on “Load Google Fonts” under noticeH → Settings → Display & Styling.

  • What it is used for: displaying notice boards in the font family chosen in the settings.
  • What is sent and when: when a visitor opens a page with a notice board, their browser requests the font stylesheet and font files from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com. Google receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details with that request. No other data is sent.
  • Service provider: Google LLC. Terms of service · Privacy policy

All other assets, including Font Awesome, Swiper and AOS, are bundled with the plugin and served from your own site.

Third-Party Libraries

noticeH bundles these GPL-compatible libraries locally. The minified files are the unmodified upstream releases; human-readable source is at the links below.

  • Font Awesome Free 7.3.1 – Icons CC BY 4.0, fonts SIL OFL 1.1, code MIT – https://github.com/FortAwesome/Font-Awesome
  • Swiper 14.4.0 – MIT – https://github.com/nolimits4web/swiper
  • AOS (Animate On Scroll) 2.3.4 – MIT – https://github.com/michalsnik/aos
sections.installation:
1. In Plugins → Add New, search for “noticeH”, or upload the ZIP. You can also copy the noticeh folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate noticeH.
  3. Add notices under noticeH → Add New Notice, or import the sample notices from noticeH → Settings → Advanced & Caching.
  4. Add the noticeH Board block, or the [noticeh_board] shortcode, to any page or post.
sections.faq:
How do I display the notice board on a page?

Add the noticeH Board block, or the shortcode [noticeh_board], to any page or post. Use [noticeh_board layout="table"] to pick a layout: card, table, list, timeline, slider or ticker. The Shortcode Guide & Reference tab in the settings lists every option.

Can I show notices as a scrolling news ticker?

Yes. Use [noticeh_board layout="ticker"]. Hovering a notice shows a preview card; you can turn the preview off in the settings.

How do I pin an important notice to the top?

Tick Pin Notice as Sticky when editing the notice. Pinned notices are listed first and get a badge and a coloured border.

What happens when a notice expires?

You choose in noticeH → Settings → Notice Expiry: hide expired notices from visitors, keep them in the archive, or move them to the trash automatically.

Can I attach PDF files to a notice?

Yes. Pick files from the Media Library, or paste a link to a file on Google Drive, Dropbox or another site. Visitors see download buttons on the notice.

Does it work with Elementor, Divi or other page builders?

Yes. Put the [noticeh_board] shortcode in the page builder’s shortcode element. noticeH does not depend on any page builder. It was tested with Elementor, Beaver Builder and SiteOrigin Page Builder, and works in any builder that has a shortcode or HTML element.

Does it work with my other plugins and my theme?

noticeH was tested with the 60 most-installed plugins on WordPress.org, including WooCommerce, Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Jetpack, Wordfence, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Super Cache, Autoptimize and UpdraftPlus. It was also tested with popular themes, among them Astra, Kadence, GeneratePress, OceanWP, Blocksy, Hello Elementor and the default Twenty Twenty themes. Boards, the slider and the ticker kept working with caching and file-merging plugins switched on.

noticeH only loads its styles and scripts on pages that show a notice board, so it adds nothing to the rest of your site.

Can I import notices from a spreadsheet?

Yes. Go to noticeH → Import / Export, download the sample CSV, fill it in and import it. You can also export all notices to CSV.

Can I change the design colours?

Yes. Go to noticeH → Settings → Display & Styling to set colours for titles, text, badges, buttons and backgrounds.

Can I import the same CSV file again after editing it?

Yes. Rows are matched to existing notices by their Ref Number, so importing an edited export updates those notices instead of creating copies. Rows without a Ref Number are added as new notices. To add every row as new, untick “Update notices that have the same reference number” before importing.

What happens to my notices if I delete the plugin?

Your notices, their categories, tags and attached files stay in the database and the Media Library. Deleting the plugin only removes its settings and cached data, and you can keep the settings too with the “Keep the plugin settings when the plugin is deleted” option under Settings → Advanced. Install noticeH again and the notices are back.
sections.changelog:
1.1.25

  • Changed: notice boards filter, search and change page without reloading the page, in every layout; the browser’s Back and Forward buttons and direct links keep working.
  • Fixed: page 2 of the notice archive no longer shows “not found”; the print button is always visible; the timeline circles sit exactly on the line.
  • Changed: stricter escaping of all front-end output.

1.1.19

  • Fixed: saving settings with a tampered colour value no longer causes a server error.
  • Fixed: with “Hide completely”, an expired notice now also answers 404 at its own address and is left out of site search.
  • Fixed: uninstalling on a multisite network cleans the settings of every site.
  • Fixed: very long unbroken text and wide tables no longer widen the page on phones.
  • Changed: “posts_per_page” in the shortcode is capped at 100.
  • Removed: the “Enable cache” and “Cache duration” settings, which had no effect.
  • Removed: the “Advanced Custom CSS” setting, as the WordPress.org directory does not allow plugins to save custom CSS. Use Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS instead.

1.1.18

  • Changed: noticeH’s styles, script and Font Awesome icons load only on pages that show a notice board or notice. Other pages of your site no longer load them. Boards in widgets, page builders and templates still load what they need.
  • Fixed: an impossible year or month in a board’s filter address no longer writes a notice to the PHP error log.

1.1.17

  • Security hardening: uploaded file fields and a few request values are cleaned as soon as they are read.

1.1.16

  • Changed: importing a CSV again no longer creates copies. A row whose Ref Number matches one existing notice updates that notice; rows without a Ref Number are added as new notices. Untick “Update notices that have the same reference number” on the import screen to add every row as new.

1.1.15

  • Fixed: pinned notices always appear first. Notices without a pinned setting (for example imported from a CSV without an “Is Sticky” column) could be listed above them.
  • Fixed: sorting by priority lists urgent, then important, then normal notices, and keeps notices that have no priority set. It used to sort the words alphabetically.
  • Fixed: the REST API applies the documented orderby parameter (date, title, modified, priority).
  • Fixed: the Copy link button on a notice shows a “Link copied” message. It copied the link but showed nothing and logged an error.
  • Fixed: CSV exports open in Excel with Bangla, Arabic and accented text intact.
  • Fixed: sorting the Priority and Expiry Date columns in the notices list puts notices without a value in a consistent place.

1.1.14

  • Changed: the bundled Swiper slider library is updated from 11.0.5 to 14.4.0.
  • Changed: the bundled Font Awesome Free icons are updated from 6.5.1 to 7.3.1.
  • Removed: the Font Awesome .ttf font files. Every browser WordPress supports uses the .woff2 files, and Font Awesome 7 no longer ships .ttf. The plugin is about 700 KB smaller.
  • Changed: the uninstall option is now called “Keep the plugin settings when the plugin is deleted” and explains that notices are never removed when the plugin is deleted.
  • Changed: the LICENSE file contains the full GPL v2 text.

1.1.13

  • Security: the layout option of the shortcode and block only accepts the six built-in layouts, and templates can no longer be loaded from outside the plugin’s or theme’s template folders.
  • Security: a password-protected notice no longer shows its attachments, external link or external file until the password is entered.
  • Security: the ticker’s loop label is inserted as text, and exported CSV cells can no longer run as spreadsheet formulas.
  • Fixed: “Clear Sample Notices” only removes the six sample notices. It used to remove every notice whose reference number started with NOT-2026-.
  • Fixed: turning on “Homepage Auto-Injection” could crash the home page. The ticker is now added once.
  • Fixed: the [noticeh_single id="123"] shortcode shows the notice inside the page instead of a second page header and footer.
  • Fixed: the notices RSS feed is valid XML and leaves out expired notices when they are set to be hidden.
  • Fixed: the documented shortcode options loop_label and orderby="title", "modified" and "rand" now work.
  • Fixed: CSV import no longer shows PHP 8.4 notices, reads files saved by Excel, and reports rows that could not be saved.
  • Fixed: the Priority and Expiry Date columns in the notices list can be sorted.
  • Fixed: on a multisite network, the daily cleanup of expired notices is scheduled on every site.
  • Fixed: uninstalling also removes the category cache option WordPress keeps for the plugin.
  • Changed: layouts and template parts can be overridden from your-theme/noticeh/, for example noticeh/layouts/card.php.
  • Changed: the block’s settings are translatable and the block preview in the editor is styled like the front end.

Earlier versions

noticeH 1.0 to 1.1.12 were released before the plugin was listed on WordPress.org.
